name: renderdoc-for-vscode
description: View and analyze RenderDoc capture (.rdc) files in VS Code

chatParticipants.name: renderdoc
chatParticipants.description: Analyze GPU captures — draw calls, shaders, textures, pipeline state, and performance

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_openCapture
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Resolve the RenderDoc capture to analyze in this window. If a capture is already loaded, returns it. Otherwise it can load a provided filePath or the active/open .rdc tab. Call this BEFORE workspace file scans or terminal commands when the user says 'this capture' or asks for capture analysis and no capture is loaded yet.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Loads the current RenderDoc capture for local analysis.

filePath.description: Optional absolute path to a .rdc capture file. If omitted, the tool tries the active/open .rdc tab in this window.

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_getSelectionContext
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get what the user is currently focused on in the RenderDoc Inspector: focused event ID, current draw call, pipeline state, and sidebar selection. Call this FIRST for any question referring to 'this/the current/the selected' draw call, event, or resource.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Returns what the user has focused in the RenderDoc Inspector.

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_getCaptureInfo
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get metadata about the currently loaded RenderDoc capture file (.rdc), including graphics API, GPU driver, capture version, and file sections. Call this early when API or driver context matters, but prefer getFrameSummary first for frame structure or bottleneck questions.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reads metadata about the current capture.

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_getDrawCalls
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get the list of GPU draw calls/events in the captured frame with event IDs, names, index/instance counts. Prefer getFrameSummary first for broad frame overview or performance questions, then use this with a narrower filter, marker subtree, or event range instead of dumping the whole frame when possible. Supports multiple filters: 'filter' (name substring), 'markerFilter' (limit to a marker subtree), 'excludeMarkers' (leaf events only), 'onlyDrawCalls' (actual GPU ops), 'eventIdMin'/'eventIdMax' (event ID range).
languageModelTools.userDescription: Lists draw calls in the capture.

markerFilter.description: Only include events inside a marker group whose name contains this string (case-insensitive)

excludeMarkers.description: If true, exclude marker/group nodes and return leaf events only

onlyDrawCalls.description: If true, only return actual GPU draw operations (Drawcall, Dispatch, MeshDispatch flags)

eventIdMin.description: Only include events with eventId >= this value

eventIdMax.description: Only include events with eventId <= this value

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_getActionTimings
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fetch GPU action timings on demand via the native replay bridge. Use for performance questions when timings have not been pre-fetched yet, especially after getFrameSummary or getSelectionContext identified the relevant region or focused event. After finding the hottest passes or leaf draws, continue with getEventDetails and, if needed, getShaderInfo or getPipelineState instead of stopping at a flat timing list.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Fetches GPU timings for actions in the current capture.

eventIds.description: Optional list of specific event IDs to query

markerFilter.description: Only include actions inside marker groups whose names contain this string

excludeMarkers.description: Exclude actions inside marker groups whose names contain any of these strings

onlyDrawCalls.description: If true, only include actual draw/dispatch/mesh-dispatch leaf actions

limit.description: Maximum timing rows to return (default 200, 0 = unlimited)

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_getResources
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get the list of GPU resources in the capture: textures, buffers, shaders. Use this for inventory or discovery when the target resource is not known yet; once you have a specific resource ID, prefer getResourceDetail or getTextureInfo. Paginated: default limit is 500, pass `limit`+`offset` for large captures.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Lists GPU resources in the capture.

type.description: Optional resource type filter: Texture, Buffer, Shader

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_getResourceDetail
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get detailed information about a specific GPU resource by its resource ID. Use this after selection context, getResources, or reverse lookup has identified the exact resource, and prefer it before requesting raw texture pixels or buffer bytes.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reads details for a single GPU resource.

resourceId.description: The resource ID to look up

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_getEventDetails
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get full details of a specific GPU event/draw call by its event ID, including pipeline state if native bridge is available. This is the default first stop for a specific EID after selection context, timings, or frame summary have identified the event. Use it before deeper shader- or state-specific inspection.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reads full details for a specific draw call event.

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_getPipelineState
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get the full GPU pipeline state at a specific draw call event, including bound shaders, textures, blend/depth state. Requires native bridge. Prefer this after getEventDetails when the question is about state, bindings, render targets, or fixed-function configuration rather than raw shader code.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reads the GPU pipeline state at a draw call.

eventId.description: The event ID to get pipeline state for

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_getShaderSource
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get shader source code (GLSL/HLSL) at a specific draw call event. Optionally specify shader stage (vertex, fragment, compute). Use this only when the user explicitly wants shader code or source-level stage analysis; prefer getShaderInfo when bindings or constant buffers matter too.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reads shader source at a draw call.

stage.description: Shader stage: vertex, fragment, geometry, compute

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_getShaderInfo
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get a higher-level shader summary at a draw call event by aggregating shader metadata/source, bound textures/samplers, and decoded constant buffer contents for one or more stages. Prefer this over calling shaderSource + pipelineState + constant buffer inspection separately when analyzing a shader stage, especially after getEventDetails or a timing hotspot identified the target EID.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reads aggregated shader source, bindings, and constant buffers at a draw call.

stage.description: Optional shader stage filter: vertex, fragment, pixel, geometry, hull, domain, tessControl, tessEval, compute

includeSource.description: Include full source files / disassembly when available. Defaults to true when stage is specified.

includeConstantBuffers.description: Include decoded constant buffer contents (default true)

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_findProjectImplementation
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Find likely project-side implementation files for a RenderDoc issue by searching the open workspace with shader names, pass/marker names, or a specific event ID. Use this after a hot EID, suspicious pass, or shader has already been identified in the capture to bridge from analysis back to shader files and C# render-pass code.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Searches the open project for shader/pass implementation candidates related to the current capture.

eventId.description: Optional event ID to derive shader names and pass/marker names from

shaderName.description: Optional explicit shader name or shader file name to search

passName.description: Optional explicit pass or marker name to search in C# project code

additionalTerms.description: Additional search terms to include in project lookup

limit.description: Maximum results to return per category (default 12)

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_getTextureInfo
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get information about textures in the capture. Optionally filter by texture ID. Use this after selection context or resource identification to inspect texture metadata before reverse tracing or pixel-data fetches.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reads information about textures.

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_analyzeFrame
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Perform a comprehensive analysis of the captured frame: draw call statistics, resource usage, potential performance issues. Use this when the user wants a broad issue scan rather than a narrow question about one selected event or resource.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Analyzes the captured frame holistically.

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_getMeshData
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get mesh data for a specific draw event and stage, including topology, vertex attributes, and a bounded sample of rows. Use this after a hot event has been identified to inspect geometry pressure, vertex input layout, or post-VS output.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reads mesh data for a specific event.

stage.description: Mesh stage: vsin, vsout, or gsout

maxVertices.description: Maximum vertices to return in the sampled rows. Default: 32

instance.description: Instance index for instanced draws. Default: 0

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_getFrameSummary
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get a concise structural overview of the frame: top-level render passes/markers with child counts, leaf draw/dispatch/clear counts, and GPU capture statistics. Use this FIRST for frame overview, pass layout, render flow, or bottleneck questions before getDrawCalls. After this identifies the hot region, move to getActionTimings or specific EIDs instead of expanding the whole frame blindly.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Returns a high-level summary of the frame structure.

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_findDrawsByShader
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Find all draw call event IDs that use a given shader (by name or entry point substring). Builds a reverse index on first call — may be slow for large captures. Use to trace which draws use a specific shader.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reverse-searches draws by bound shader name.

shaderName.description: Shader name or entry point substring to search (case-insensitive)

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_findDrawsByTexture
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Find all draw call event IDs that sample a given texture (by name substring). Builds a reverse index on first call. Use to trace where a specific texture is read.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reverse-searches draws by bound texture name.

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_findDrawsByResourceId
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Find all draw call event IDs that bind a specific resource ID. Useful for tracing exact resource usage by ID.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reverse-searches draws by resource ID.

resourceId.description: Resource ID string to find (exact match)

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_getTextureData
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Sample a texture at a specific event and mip level, returning a base64-encoded PNG. Use this only when pixel inspection is necessary after the target texture has already been identified. Keep requests narrow with a specific eventId, mip, and channel when possible.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reads texture pixel data as a base64 PNG.

eventId.description: Event ID at which to sample the texture (0 = end of frame). Default: 0

languageModelTools.name: renderdoc_getBufferContents
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Read raw bytes from a GPU buffer resource and return them base64-encoded. Use to inspect vertex buffers, index buffers, constant/uniform buffers, storage buffers, etc. Identify the exact buffer first, start with a small slice by default, and use offset+len to page through larger buffers. Max 65536 bytes per call.
languageModelTools.userDescription: Reads raw bytes from a GPU buffer resource.

offset.description: Byte offset into the buffer. Default: 0

len.description: Number of bytes to read. Default: 4096. Max: 65536

eventId.description: Event ID at which to read the buffer (0 = end of frame). Default: 0

commands.title: Show RenderDoc For VSCode MCP Info

viewsWelcome.contents: Use the Capture Target workflow to 1) choose a target, 2) launch or attach, and 3) capture from the live session.

No RDC capture file opened.
[Open Capture File](command:renderdoc.openCapture)
[Open Inspector](command:renderdoc.openInspector)

renderdoc.commandTimeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds for renderdoccmd execution, such as thumbnail fallback commands.

renderdoc.alwaysReplayLocally.description: When a capture suggests remote replay because it was created on another platform, skip the prompt and continue with local replay.

renderdoc.maliOfflineCompilerPath.description: Optional path to the Mali Offline Compiler executable (malioc.exe). Configure only if you want Mali shader analysis.

renderdoc.mcpServer.enabled.description: Expose the optional local RenderDoc For VSCode MCP endpoint for other VS Code AI clients. The extension itself uses its built-in RenderDoc tools directly.

renderdoc.mcpServer.port.description: TCP port used by the local RenderDoc For VSCode MCP server. Change this only if the default port conflicts with another process.
